sections.heading: Create a contact
sections.snippet: Set CONTACT_NUMBER to the contact’s phone number in E.164 format. The public collection uses the original API host and sends contact fields
sections.text: Set CONTACT_NUMBER to the contact’s phone number in E.164 format. The public collection uses the original API host and sends contact fields in the query string of a POST request. Set ALIVE5_ORG_NAME and ACCOUNT_ID to your own account values. Creating a contact does not establish SMS consent. POST /contact/create-new curl -G -X POST https://api.alive5.com/public/1.0/contact/create-new \ -H "X-A5-APIKEY: $ALIVE5_KEY" \ --data-urlencode "email=alex@example.com" \ --data-urlencode "org_name=$ALIVE5_ORG_NAME" \ --data-urlencode "first_name=Alex" \ --data-urlencode "phone_mobile=$CONTACT_NUMBER" \ --data-urlencode "last_name=Example" \ --data-urlencode "account_id=$ACCOUNT_ID" \ --data-urlencode "title=Customer" \ --data-urlencode "company=Example company"

sections.heading: Update a contact
sections.snippet: Replace YOUR_CONTACT_ID with an ID returned by your contact list and YOUR_TAG_NAME with a tag label from your account. Pass tag labels in ta
sections.text: Replace YOUR_CONTACT_ID with an ID returned by your contact list and YOUR_TAG_NAME with a tag label from your account. Pass tag labels in tags. Send the changes as JSON to the original API host. PUT /contact/update-contact curl -X PUT https://api.alive5.com/public/1.0/contact/update-contact \ -H "X-A5-APIKEY: $ALIVE5_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data '{"crm_id":"YOUR_CONTACT_ID","tags":["YOUR_TAG_NAME"]}' Confirm the write. This endpoint can return code 200 and a populated error in the same response. Re-read the contact before treating an update as applied.

sections.heading: Check three fields
sections.snippet: A call is accepted only when the HTTP status and response code are successful and error is empty. Some endpoints nest a second envelope insi
sections.text: A call is accepted only when the HTTP status and response code are successful and error is empty. Some endpoints nest a second envelope inside data, so check that too. is-ok.js // Pass the HTTP response status: isOk(body, response.status). function isOk(body, httpStatus) { if (!(httpStatus >= 200 && httpStatus < 300)) return false; if (!body || typeof body !== "object" || Array.isArray(body)) return false; if (body.code == null) return false; for (let part = body; part; ) { if (part.code != null && !(Number(part.code) >= 200 && Number(part.code) < 300)) return false; const error = part.error; const empty = error == null || (typeof error === "object" && Object.keys(error).length === 0); if (!empty) return false; const next = part.data; part = next && typeof next === "object" && !Array.isArray(next) && ("code" in next || "error" in next) ? next : null; } return true; }

sections.heading: Process new messages
sections.snippet: Keep a record of the messages you have processed. Use a stable message ID when available; otherwise count occurrences of each (thread, sende
sections.text: Keep a record of the messages you have processed. Use a stable message ID when available; otherwise count occurrences of each (thread, sender, timestamp, content) tuple, as the Node-RED node does. Track how many occurrences you have processed rather than treating the tuple as unique: separate messages can have identical values. Follow the response pagination to read additional pages. sections.heading: Consent and opt-out
sections.snippet: Register for 10DLC. US local numbers need an approved campaign before outbound texts are delivered. Collect website consent. Use HTTPS and c
sections.text: Register for 10DLC. US local numbers need an approved campaign before outbound texts are delivered. Collect website consent. Use HTTPS and consent/privacy language. When the phone field is required, include an initially unchecked “Opt-in to receive texts?” checkbox. Honor opt-outs immediately. Process STOP, END, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, and QUIT regardless of case or punctuation. Send one final confirmation, then stop messaging. Use double opt-in in bot flows. Ask the recipient to reply YES. Without that reply, they are not opted in to promotional messaging. Keep consent records. Download the opt-in/out logs as CSV from Reporting → Logs → Opt In, Opt Out logs. For repeated events from one number, use the latest event. Sample message: “Reply STOP to opt out. Reply HELP for help.”

sections.heading: Send an SMS
sections.snippet: Configure alive5 send sms and pass it a message with these values: Node field or message property Value Account Your alive5-config connectio
sections.text: Configure alive5 send sms and pass it a message with these values: Node field or message property Value Account Your alive5-config connection. SMS line The Alive5 business number to send from. Sending user A user assigned to the selected line. To / msg.to The recipient in E.164 format, such as +14155550123. msg.to overrides the node’s To field. msg.payload A non-empty string containing the SMS text. On success, msg.payload becomes an object with message_id and any available message_status, thread_id, From, To, direction, and message_content fields. This confirms API acceptance, not delivery. Connect a Catch node to handle failures. If a send times out, check conversation history before retrying; a failed response does not prove the SMS was not sent.

sections.heading: Receive texts
sections.snippet: Add alive5 sms in, select your account and SMS line, and set Poll seconds. The default is 30 seconds, with a minimum of 1 second. The next i
sections.text: Add alive5 sms in, select your account and SMS line, and set Poll seconds. The default is 30 seconds, with a minimum of 1 second. The next interval starts after the current request finishes. The first successful poll records a silent baseline without emitting messages. Later polls output new incoming texts in msg.payload: Payload field Value message The incoming text. from_phone The sender’s phone number. business_line The selected Alive5 SMS number. thread_id The Alive5 conversation identifier. received_at The message timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format. Polling limits State resets on restart or redeploy. The API returns a recent conversation window, so downtime is not backfilled and messages can be missed between polls. Messages with an older timestamp than one already seen are skipped.

sections.text: Run List channels and users. In data.Items, choose an SMS channel whose channel_label is your business phone number. Copy its channel_id and an assigned agent's user_id. Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' https://alive5.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self'; Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self' 'nonce-RANDOM_NONCE_GENERATED' https://alive5.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self'; For the nonce variant, generate a fresh nonce in each request handler and pass it to the template: Node.js · per-request nonce const crypto = require('crypto'); // Inside your request handler: const nonce = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64'); reply.header('Content-Security-Policy', `script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' https://alive5.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self';`); reply.locals.nonce = nonce; Use the same nonce in the inline script’s opening tag and load Alive5 scripts over HTTPS: HTML · Opening tag with nonce <script type="text/javascript" nonce="{{nonce}}">

sections.text: Use the Alive5 module for Drupal 10 ↗ to embed the widget with page, role, and content-type display rules. You need an Alive5 live-chat/AI account and a Widget ID. Find your Widget ID In Alive5, open Widgets → View → The Code. Copy the value of data-widget_code_id. Open the module configuration In Drupal, go to Configuration → System → Alive5. Enter the ID Paste the value into Widget ID. To prefill visitor details, see Pass visitor data.
